scenes.headline: How Beam runs 23B of 501B per token
scenes.sub: Reflection's open MoE, announced before its weights ship.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Peda! Beam stores five hundred and one billion parameters, and runs twenty-three billion of them per token.

scenes.text: A sparse model, pushed hard with asynchronous RL, that reaches its scores while generating far fewer tokens.
scenes.say: A sparse model, trained with a huge asynchronous reinforcement learning run, that scores while writing far fewer tokens.

steps.say: Each block starts with attention. Some blocks see a local window, others the whole context.
Then a router sends the token to a few small experts out of many. So little of the model runs.
Norms on both sides and a full precision residual keep the signal steady through fifty-two blocks.
Agents pull tasks from nearly a million environments, with about a hundred and ten thousand rollouts running at once.
Every generated token is tagged with the weight version that wrote it.
The trainer learns from finished rollouts while generation continues, correcting for stale tokens.
New weights reach the fleet in about twelve seconds. Some samples are a day old, and training stays stable.

scenes.title: What the efficiency chart counts
scenes.text: FLOPs = 2 x active params x tokens

parts.say: Reflection's efficiency axis is a formula. Two, times active parameters, times generated tokens.
So a model wins by being smaller per token, and by writing less. Prefill and attention are left out.

scenes.title: Terminal Bench 2.1, tokens per attempt
scenes.say: Read off their chart, Beam scores higher on Terminal Bench with under a third of the tokens.

scenes.label: GPU-hours of RL, more than pretraining used
scenes.say: And the cost moved. Four weeks of RL on ten and a half thousand GPUs is more GPU time than all of pretraining.

scenes.text: Beam's efficiency is tokens per task scaled by active size, and its biggest training bill was RL.
scenes.mark: tokens per task scaled by active size
scenes.say: Remember what the efficiency means. Tokens per task, scaled by active size. And the weights are not out yet.
A small slice of a big model. Asynchronous RL at scale. An efficiency number that counts generated tokens.
